summary: This paper introduces TIPS, a topological framework that treats the contextual hidden states of prompt tokens in large language models as a point cloud to analyze and steer responses to ill-posed questions. By extracting seven descriptors from zero- and one-dimensional persistent homology, the method achieves improved performance in both binary and fine-grained ill-posedness classification. Furthermore, topology-conditioned activation steering significantly increases the rate of appropriate clarification or abstention responses.

chk_problem.value: Large language models struggle with ill-posed questions (such as those involving ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements) because existing work treats LLM reasoning as a black box.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Ill-posed questions, including those involving ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements, may admit no valid answer or multiple plausible answers, posing a significant challenge for large language models (LLMs) despite their otherwise strong performance.

We evaluate eight models from four families using five split seeds (0–4), with 70/10/20
train/validation/test splits. Layer selection is performed separately for each split using validation
data. Table 1 reports macro-F1 as mean ± sample standard deviation across the five splits.
Table 1 shows that the seven selected-layer H0 and H1 descriptors achieve higher average macroF1 than AEN and the strongest single prompt-based baseline on both classification tasks, although
performance varies across models. On the binary AmbigQA task, averaged equally across eight
models, our topology-based classifier achieves 78.60% macro-F1, compared with 75.51% for AEN
and 54.06% for few-shot prompting, the strongest prompt-based baseline on average. On CLAMBER nine-way classification, our method achieves an average macro-F1 of 39.44%, compared with
36.64% for AEN and 35.81% for few-shot prompting. These results suggest that a compact, sevendimensional topological representation captures ill-posedness-relevant structure in internal question
representations, including information useful for fine-grained subtype classification beyond binary
detection.
